question: Who produced the document of Mahzar at the instance of Akbar?
solution:
The correct answer is __Shaikh Mubarak__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Akbar issued a Declaration or Mahzar.
 
• Mahzar means pronouncement, declaration or an opinion.
 
• It also implies petition.
 
• He removed the Chief Preacher at Fatehpur Sikri and himself mounted the Pulpit of Jama Masjib, Fatehpur Sikri on June 22, 1579 and read the Khutba in his own names as the prophet and caliphs. 
 
• The Khutba was composed in verse by Faizi.
 
• Mahzar was issued in September 1579 and it was prepared by Sheikh Mubarak.
 
• Mahzar was signed by all the prominent Muslim theologians and divines of the Mughal empire.
 
• It was also signed by Makhdum-ul-Mulk and Abdun Nabi, although they were known to be bitter critics of Akbar's liberal religious policy.
 
• As instituted under the Mahzar, it was decided that Akbar would have the right to be the supreme arbiter or interpreter of Islamic laws, and he could decide in the matter of differing opinions on all religious questions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abul Fazl** ​

 
 
• **Abul Fazl** (1547–1602) was a prominent scholar, historian, and one of the most notable figures in the Mughal Empire during the reign of Emperor Akbar.
 
• He is best known for his work as the author of the **Akbarnama**, a detailed historical account of Akbar’s reign, and for his role in Akbar's court.
 
• Abul Fazl was a trusted advisor and one of the "Navaratnas" (Nine Gems) in Akbar’s court. 
 
 
 
• **Abdun Nabi**
 
 
• **​Abdun Nabi** was a prominent figure during the reign of **Emperor Akbar** in the Mughal Empire, though his life and role are less widely documented than some of the other notable figures of that period.
 
• The name **Abdun Nabi** could refer to multiple historical figures, but the most well-known context for **Abdun Nabi** is in the **administrative and military domains** of the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Faizi ****​**
 
 
• Faizi was a highly regarded Persian poet and a scholar of Arabic, Persian, and Indian languages. He was deeply involved in the literary and intellectual activities of Akbar’s court.
 
• He was well-versed in Persian literature and made significant contributions to it. His work includes poetry that blended classical Persian traditions with the Mughal cultural environment.
 
• He was also a mentor to **Abul Fazl**, and their intellectual contributions are often discussed together in the context of the flourishing of Mughal culture.
